Why gluten-free bread goes wrong

Three things that trip up most home bakers

Gluten is what gives wheat bread its stretch and structure. Take it out, and you need to solve for that some other way — that's the whole game.

01

Loaves that collapse or stay gummy in the center because there's no gluten network to trap gas and set the crumb.

02

A single flour swapped 1:1 for wheat flour, when gluten-free baking actually needs a blend of starches, flours, and a binder.

03

Dry, crumbly texture from too little hydration — gluten-free doughs generally need more liquid than wheat doughs, not less.

Getting started

How to use this collection

01

Start with a beginner loaf

Cassava Bread or Cornbread are forgiving places to learn how gluten-free dough should look and feel.

02

Follow the amounts closely

Gluten-free doughs are less forgiving than wheat doughs, so stick to the listed weights the first time you make a loaf.

03

Work up to the grain-based loaves

Teff, quinoa, and chia breads ask more of you, but the technique carries over once the basics click.

Questions

Frequently asked

Do I need a gluten-free flour blend, or can I use one flour?+

Most recipes here use a blend of a whole-grain flour (rice, sorghum, teff) with a starch (tapioca, cassava) for structure. A few, like the almond and coconut loaf, use fewer flours by design. The recipe card tells you which.

Why do some recipes use potato or sweet potato?+

Mashed root vegetables add moisture and hold the crumb together, which helps offset the lack of gluten in the dough.

Can I make these dairy-free too?+

Most recipes already lean on coconut oil, coconut milk, or olive oil rather than butter or dairy milk, so they're naturally close to dairy-free as written.

Why is my loaf gummy in the middle even after baking?+

Usually it's underbaked. Gluten-free loaves often need a higher internal temperature than wheat bread — check with a thermometer rather than a toothpick.

How should I store gluten-free bread?+

It stales faster than wheat bread. Slice and freeze what you won't eat in a day or two, and toast straight from frozen.
